added.title: Research Software Engineer
added.description:
Job Type

Regular

Overview

RAND is seeking a Research Software Engineer to work in a multidisciplinary environment, collaborating closely with research staff and analysts across a variety of domains, including health care, education, national security, and social and economic wellbeing. They are expected to develop an understanding of the research topic and apply their programming and analytic skills to research needs, working as part of a small team of software engineers with guidance from more experienced team members alongside domain experts and research staff.

Research Software Engineers support research projects by assisting with gathering requirements from users, contributing to the design of software products with researchers, implementing designs in code, and iterating with users and researchers to ensure functional and quality requirements are met. Technical needs vary by project, so the position requires a generalist mindset, with interest in gaining experience across web, mobile, desktop, database, modeling & simulation, and data analytics paradigms. Candidates are expected to have a foundational knowledge of software development principles, and architecture and development of secure, performant AI-driven applications and platforms.

Required Qualifications

High-level proficiency in Python, plus working experience with at least one other language or platform relevant to applied research work — web (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript), database (e.g., PostgreSQL, MongoDB), or analytic (e.g., R, Julia)
Experience developing or contributing to building applications on top of LLMs or other foundation models, including context design, retrieval augmentation, tool use, or agentic workflows
Familiarity with the capabilities, limitations, and common failure modes of current AI models and interest in developing sound judgments about their use them in software applications.
Familiarity with debugging, documenting and testing software, including both conventional testing (unit, integration, acceptance) and methods for assessing the outputs of nondeterministic, AI-enabled systems
Exposure to deploying and maintaining applications
Ability to turn ambiguous, evolving research needs into working software in close collaboration with non-engineers, and a willingness to pick up unfamiliar tools as projects require
Strong written and verbal communication skills, and a preference for working as part of a small, collaborative, multidisciplinary team

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a research environment
Experience designing the architecture of systems in which AI is one component among several, alongside data pipelines, conventional software, and human review
Secure development practices, particularly for AI-enabled systems handling sensitive or restricted data
Web application development and UI/UX design
Large-scale data processing platforms such as Databricks

Experience

At least 1 year of hands-on experience developing generative AI applications, including experience gained through internships, research projects, or professional employment required.
At least 2 years relevant software development experience preferred.

Education

BA/BS in Computer Science or related quantitative field required.
MA/MS in Computer Science or related quantitative field strongly preferred.

Location

This position will be in a RAND office in one of the following locations: Santa Monica, CA; Washington D.C.; or Pittsburgh, PA

Security Clearance

Candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. Please note that U.S. citizenship is required to obtain and maintain a government security clearance. Candidates with an active U.S. security clearance are preferred.

Salary Range:
$36.40 - $54.03 per hour

RAND considers a variety of factors when formulating an offer, including but not limited to, the specific role and associated responsibilities; a candidate’s work experience, education/training, skills, expertise; and internal equity. This position is overtime eligible. In addition, RAND provides strong benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, paid time-off and more.

Equal Opportunity Employer

This role is responsible for developing embedded software for industrial motion controllers, assisting in achieving sales growth and the success of the corporate business. If you are a hardworking Mechanical, Electrical, or Computer Engineer, this may be the perfect opportunity for you.

The Embedded Software Engineer
, based in our San Francisco office, designs, implements and tests software for mechatronic systems. This role makes an important impact on the success of the corporate business. The successful candidate will participate in all phases of development, including specification, detailed design, testing and design review.

Qualifications

B.S. or M.S. (preferred) or equivalent degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering or other mechatronics related fields
Software development project experience in professional (preferred), university or personal environment
Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem solving skills
Strong communication skills
Familiarity with object-oriented software design skills (C++ language preferred)
Familiarity with general embedded real-time operating systems (RTOS) concepts, including multi-threading, synchronization, task scheduling and priority
Familiarity with Linux operating system
Familiarity with software development tools such as gcc, Git, ALM systems
Ability to comprehend and contribute to software design documents, references, and technical specifications
Ability to read and comprehend electrical schematics, and troubleshoot hardware problems on prototype boards
Practical experience with using electrical test equipment such as multimeters, oscilloscopes, chart recorders, logic analyzers, etc

Job Duties

Design, implement, document and test embedded software in C++ for motion controllers
Participate in all design phases including gathering of software requirements, specification, detailed design and testing.
Facilitate product release cycle by supporting testing, executing bugfixes, and updating documentation

Design, implement, and maintain developer tools and testing systems
Troubleshoot hardware problems on prototype boards and communicate technical issues with hardware designers.
Support Product Management in software technical manual creation and providing software files to Product/Manufacturing/Quality Engineering.
Support customer software development activities. Provide software updates, documentation, training and answer technical questions.
Occasional travel to other Yaskawa facilities worldwide (USA, Germany, Japan) for training or participation in joint development projects.

We offer the opportunity to experience the excitement, challenge and rewards of working in an entrepreneurial, fast growing, and industry-leading company where you will be challenged to manage projects and apply your skills to a wide variety of applications.

added.description:
Who We Are

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About The Role

The Platform IoT team runs the device cloud that keeps Motive devices connected. We own the full path between devices and the cloud, including provisioning and identity, messaging, firmware updates and certificates, configuration delivery, data ingestion, and monitoring. Our platform supports more than 1 million connected devices across North America and Europe.

As a Software Engineer on the team, you’ll build and monitor the services behind these systems and own projects end-to-end—from design and well-tested code to safe deployment and production operations. You’ll work with backend, firmware, and product engineers to solve the challenges of keeping a large fleet secure, up to date, and reporting data. We’re looking for an infrastructure or cloud engineer with strong engineering fundamentals, depth in at least one of our focus areas, and a commitment to production ownership.

This role is based in San Francisco and requires two days (Tuesdays/Thursdays) per week in the office.

What You’ll Do

Design, build, and deploy reliable, maintainable, and performant services in Go and Ruby, AWS Lambda functions, and Terraform-managed infrastructure.
Build and monitor the platform that teams use to roll out firmware and configuration to devices.
Improve dashboards, alerts, and observability so the team can identify and address issues proactively.
Support new hardware launches, including provisioning, factory enablement, and related device-side features.
Build and improve Kafka, Flink, and MQTT data ingestion pipelines for device telemetry and files.
Participate in the team’s on-call rotation and improve runbooks and tooling to make on-call easier.
Help manage technical debt by consolidating approaches and making pragmatic decisions about what to improve and when.
Write clear design documents, provide thoughtful code reviews, and keep documentation current for the systems you own.
Collaborate effectively with teammates across time zones.

What We’re Looking For

4+ years of professional software engineering experience, including building and operating backend or distributed services in production.
Proficiency with AI tools and automation, including AI-assisted coding.
Strong coding skills in Go or a similar language (such as Java, Python, or Rust) and a willingness to work in Go.
Experience building and operating services on AWS, including serverless services such as Lambda and infrastructure as code such as Terraform.
Understanding of networking and security fundamentals, including TLS, certificates, and authentication between services and devices.
Experience with monitoring, logging, and alerting, and a habit of instrumenting the systems you build.
Ability to debug issues across system boundaries and explain findings in plain language.
Clear written communication skills, including the ability to write design documents that teammates in other time zones can act on.
Preferred: Experience with Ruby.
Preferred: Working knowledge of messaging and streaming systems such as MQTT and Kafka.
Preferred: Experience with connected devices, IoT platforms, or firmware delivery.
Preferred: Experience with Kubernetes, stream processing frameworks such as Flink, or factory provisioning flows for hardware products.

Pay Transparency

Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Learn more about our benefits by visiting Motive Perks & Benefits

$135,000—$185,000 USD

added.description:
Akima Infrastructure Services, LLC (AIS), is actively seeking Engineering, Professional, Technical, and administrative support personnel as part of our staff augmentation team supporting the Department of Energy at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) located in Richland, WA.

Successful candidates will be employees of AIS, a premier government contractor charged with employing highly motivated and well-qualified personnel who can advance PNNL’s core mission to ensure a safe, secure, and reliable U.S. nuclear deterrent, which is essential to national security. Though employed by AIS, the employee will take day-to-day direction and assignments from PNNL staff employed directly by the security complex. Pay, benefits, Human Resources, and Employment Management functions are provided by AIS.

Qualified applicants must be a US citizen, at least 18 years of age, and able to meet pre-employment requirements including any required physicals, drug screen, and/or background investigation to satisfy clearance requirements from the Department of Energy.

To join our team of outstanding professionals, apply today!

Responsibilities

The focus of this work is to design, build, test, and enhance software systems that support laboratory operations. These are full-stack roles involving development across React user interfaces and C#/.NET services. Frontend responsibilities will include building accessible, responsive, and maintainable components, implementing application workflows, managing client-side data and state, and integrating with APIs. Backend responsibilities will include developing domain and application logic, integrations, automated tests, and data-access components using Entity Framework Core and Microsoft SQL Server. The contractor will also design data models, implement and optimize queries, manage schema changes and migrations, and build JSON:API-compliant endpoints. Work will be delivered iteratively using Agile practices, managed in Jira and GitHub, and checked into PNNL repositories daily. Deliverables will be subject to engineering review and user acceptance.

The selected developer will join an embedded team supporting and modernizing custom business information systems. The individual will work across C#/.NET backend services and React-based web applications, helping align legacy systems with current technical standards and deliver maintainable, secure, and reliable solutions. The work will also support the transition from Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) to Platform as a Service (PaaS).

Qualifications

BS Degree and five or more years of professional software development experience, including substantial full-stack application development.
Strong proficiency with C#, .NET, ASP.NET Core, object-oriented programming, and maintainable application architectures.
Strong experience with Entity Framework Core, including entity modeling, relationships, LINQ queries, change tracking, migrations, transactions, concurrency, and performance optimization.
Strong SQL skills and experience with Microsoft SQL Server, including relational database design, query optimization, indexing, data integrity, and troubleshooting.
Familiarity with the JSON:API specification, including resources, attributes, relationships, filtering, sorting, pagination, sparse fieldsets, and related-resource inclusion.
Strong proficiency with React and modern frontend development, including JavaScript or TypeScript, component design, state management, API integration, HTML, CSS, responsive design, accessibility, and frontend testing.
Proficiency with an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, including its effective use for codebase analysis, implementation, refactoring, test development, and documentation, with appropriate human review and adherence to organizational security and data-handling requirements.
Experience working in iterative delivery environments such as Agile or Scrum.
Strong interpersonal communication skills with technical and nontechnical audiences, sound judgment, and a demonstrated commitment to professionalism and integrity
Must successfully complete Cyber Security training prior to onboarding at PNNL. This can be accomplished online through the PNNL Web Portal.

Special Requirements

Pre-employment Drug Screen - external applicants selected for this position are required to successfully complete a post- offer, pre-employment drug test.
Medical Exam(s) - Job related pre-placement medical examinations may be required for this position.
This position may require the ability to obtain and maintain a clearance from the Department of Energy. If determined as such, this position would be identified as a Workplace Substance Abuse (WSAP) testing designated position. WSAP positions require participation in an ongoing random drug testing program in addition to the pre-employment drug screen.
Any clearance requirements for this position are established by the government contract.

"This position is contingent upon contract award and funding. Applicants selected may be offered but cannot begin work until funding has been confirmed."

Job ID

2026-28844

Work Type

Remote

Pay Range

$115,000 - $155,000

Benefits

Regular - The company offers a comprehensive benefits program, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) and a range of other voluntary benefits. Paid Time Off (PTO) is offered to regular full-time and part-time employees.

Company Description

Work Where it Matters

Akima Infrastructure Services (AIS), an Akima company, is not just another staffing contractor. As an Alaska Native Corporation (ANC), our mission and purpose extend beyond our exciting federal projects as we support our shareholder communities in Alaska.

At AIS, the work you do every day makes a difference in the lives of our 15,000 Iñupiat shareholders, a group of Alaska natives from one of the most remote and harshest environments in the United States.

For our shareholders
, AIS provides support and employment opportunities and contributes to the survival of a culture that has thrived above the Arctic Circle for more than 10,000 years.

For our government customers
, AIS supports vital missions with the most in-demand and specialized skill sets in the world.

As an AIS employee
, you will be surrounded by a challenging, yet supportive work environment that is committed to innovation and diversity, two of our most important values. You will also have access to our comprehensive benefits and competitive pay in addition to growth opportunities and excellent retirement options.

A Snapshot of Your Day

As the Factory Data Engineer, you will play a critical role in building the reliable data foundation for our new Large Power Transformer factory in Charlotte, NC. You will develop and maintain data pipelines, integrations, and scalable data infrastructure that connect operational and enterprise data and make it accessible for analytics, reporting, and digital manufacturing solutions.

This role is based in Charlotte, North Carolina and closely connected to on-site operations. You will work side-by-side with manufacturing, operations, digitalization, IT data teams, system owners, and external vendors. If you enjoy solving complex integration challenges and turning fragmented factory data into dependable, well-documented data products, this role offers a unique opportunity to shape the data foundation of a factory of the future.

Build reliable data foundations by designing, developing, and maintaining scalable data ingestion pipelines and integrations for factory operations.
Connect critical data sources, integrating operational and enterprise systems including MES, SAP, PLM, IIoT connectors, APIs, and other factory platforms.
Enable the Factory Data Cloud, supporting its architecture, data flows, and dependable use as a foundation for analytics and digital solutions.
Improve data accessibility, making trusted data available to analysts, process owners, and digital use cases while supporting appropriate access controls.
Strengthen data quality and reliability by implementing quality checks, monitoring data availability, troubleshooting failures, and addressing source-system issues.
Document data assets and interfaces, maintaining clear technical documentation for pipelines, mappings, dependencies, and data definitions.
Partner across functions, working with the Digital Transformation Officer, Data Analyst, IT data teams, operations, and MES/SAP/PLM system owners to translate business needs into sustainable data solutions.
Coordinate integration delivery, managing dependencies with internal stakeholders and external vendors and proactively addressing risks caused by non-harmonized sources or access constraints.

What You Bring

5+ years of experience in data engineering, systems integration, industrial data, automation, or a related role, preferably in manufacturing or another operational environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Automation, Industrial Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Hands-on experience developing and maintaining data pipelines, integrations, and scalable data infrastructure.
Strong working knowledge of SQL, APIs, data platforms, and data integration patterns.
Experience integrating enterprise and operational systems; exposure to MES, SAP, PLM, IIoT, or factory data platforms is strongly preferred.
Experience implementing data quality checks, monitoring data availability, troubleshooting integration issues, and maintaining technical documentation.
Strong problem-solving and systems-thinking skills, with a reliable and methodical approach to delivery.
Experience with modern cloud-based data platforms (Azure preferred), AWS, Snowflake, Python, SQL, ETL/ELT frameworks, and industrial connectivity technologies such as OPC UA, MQTT, or similar platforms is preferred.

Our Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based connectivity with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This network will service tens of thousands of enterprise, data center, and government users who require reliable connectivity for critical operations.

We are seeking a Satellite Flight Software Engineer III to design, develop, and verify applications for TeraWave’s satellite flight software subsystem. This role will be instrumental in building robust, scalable flight software to support the expansion of TeraWave into a 5,408-vehicle constellation. The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer with experience developing reliable, mission-critical software for onboard spacecraft avionics systems with emphasis on command and data handling (C&DH), telecommand and telemetry processing, spacecraft time management, hardware I/O interfaces, and cybersecurity.

At Blue Origin, we’re building the future of space-based connectivity through the TeraWave satellite communications network. added.title: Sr. Radar Signal Processing Software Engineer
added.description:
Assured Space Access Technologies, Inc. is a defense and engineering firm delivering phased array, radar, RF payload, and secure communications solutions to government and prime contractor customers. We are headquartered in Irvine, California. Our Ground Based Radar team is building a mobile phased array radar, and we are adding a senior radar signal processing software engineer to the GBR Software Engineering team.

Team:
Engineering, Ground Based Radar (GBR), Software Engineering

Location:
Irvine, CA (on-site)

Employment Type:
Full-Time, Exempt

Base Salary Range:
$165,000 – $215,000 per year

Clearance:
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. An active clearance is preferred.

Position Summary

As a Senior Radar Signal Processing Software Engineer, you will turn the radar’s digitized returns into detections the tracker can use. You will own the production signal processing chain for the Ground Based Radar: pulse compression, Doppler processing, clutter filtering, CFAR, detection, and the measurement front end that feeds tracking, implemented in C++ on GPU (CUDA) or vectorized CPU targets.

You will work with the radar system designer and systems engineers who define the algorithms and performance targets, and with the radar compute platform engineers who provide the real-time framework and data movement your code runs on. Much of the work is taking MATLAB or Python reference models to fast, verified production code, then proving it on live radar data in the lab and in the field. This is a senior, hands-on seat with real ownership of the production chain.

Key Responsibilities

Signal Processing Implementation

Implement and optimize the production radar signal processing chain in C++ (CUDA or SIMD-vectorized CPU): pulse compression, Doppler filtering, clutter suppression, CFAR, and detection.
Implement the measurement front end that feeds tracking: detection clustering, range and angle estimation, and measurement formation with quality reporting.
Translate MATLAB and Python reference algorithms into production code with documented numerical equivalence and regression tests.
Meet throughput and latency budgets by profiling and tuning memory layout, kernel design, and parallelism.

Algorithm Development and Analysis

Work with the radar system designer to refine waveforms, processing parameters, and detection thresholds against the radar performance models.
Build analysis tools that evaluate detection, false alarm, and measurement accuracy performance from recorded and simulated data.
Develop simulated and recorded test data sets, including targets, clutter, and interference, for algorithm and regression testing.

Integration and Test

Integrate the processing chain onto the radar compute platform with the platform software team, using its data interfaces and scheduling framework.
Support hardware-in-the-loop testing, system integration, and field tests, including live debug and post-test data analysis.
Maintain automated builds, unit and regression tests, and documentation consistent with defense software practices.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, or a related field.
8+ years of professional software development, including at least 5 years implementing signal processing for radar, sonar, electronic warfare, or communications systems.
Strong modern C++ on Linux for high-performance or real-time applications.
Hands-on experience with GPU programming (CUDA) or SIMD-vectorized CPU optimization for signal processing.
Working knowledge of radar signal processing: matched filtering and pulse compression, Doppler processing, CFAR, and detection.
Experience converting MATLAB or Python algorithm prototypes into verified production code.
Proficiency in Python or MATLAB for analysis and test.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship.
Ability to work on site in Irvine, CA.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
Experience with phased array radar processing, such as digital beamforming, monopulse angle estimation, or space-time adaptive processing.
Experience with tracking front ends or trackers (for example, Kalman filtering and data association).
Experience with GPU libraries (cuFFT, cuBLAS) or vectorized math libraries.
Integration or field test experience with a fielded or prototype radar.
Active Secret or higher security clearance.

What we offer

Medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company matching; and paid time off.
Professional development support, including training and certifications relevant to your field.
Relocation assistance considered case by case.
Hands-on ownership of real scope in a growing defense technology company.

Equal Opportunity

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

added.description:
About Element 84

Element 84 is a woman-owned small business that works with public, private, and non-profit sector clients to develop geospatial data processing pipelines & build software that helps answer big questions about our health, our infrastructure, and our changing planet. We solve challenging problems across a wide range of industries, but our super power is cloud-based geospatial data processing, remote sensing, and Earth science systems. Our headquarters is located in Alexandria, VA and we have a satellite office in Philadelphia, PA. Element 84 also supports a large remote workforce from a variety of other states.

A Few Other Things You Should Know

Element 84's values are: We Invest in Each Other, We are Reliable, and Our Work Benefits our World.
Element 84 works on meaningful projects that are challenging—from a technical, people, and team perspective. We make an impact on large projects through our leadership and expertise, both formal and informal.
Element 84 values life outside of work. We offer parental leave for everyone and support each other through family challenges like medical problems, adoptions, and new babies.
Element 84 has had a flexible work schedule since our founding in 2010.
Element 84 is committed to fostering a culture of curiosity and respect for all individuals as we constantly strive to create a work environment where everyone feels welcome and supported.

About You

You are curious about the world, are constantly learning, driven to lead (formally or informally), and have a strong work ethic. You're interested in solving impactful problems in science, medicine, and other projects that have a societal good. You can work independently or with a team, prioritize your projects, and be effective without micromanagement.

You'll care about writing. Our team is remote, and written communication is essential. In addition to caring about a well-crafted email and a succinct conference abstract, you understand that good writing is good design and engineering.

About The Role

Element 84 is seeking an entry- to mid-level Full Stack Software Engineer with a web development background to join our talented team in creating exciting, cutting-edge web-based mapping tools for science projects that serve a variety of communities, including wildland fire management, drought monitoring, and land cover mapping.

Element 84 is a subcontractor to KBR on this program. In this role, you'll work alongside a skilled web development team that supports the USGS Earth Resources Observation and Science (EROS) Center's Integrated Science Applications Branch.

What You'll Be Working On

Developing and maintaining websites and mapping applications for visualizing and distributing geospatial data.
Developing Python scripts that produce geospatial data products.
Supporting a diverse array of technologies including, but not limited to, PHP, Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and XML.
Collaborating with a skilled web development team that supports the USGS EROS Integrated Science Applications Branch.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in software engineering or computer science.
3–5 years of recent and related work experience.
Experience with web design, administration, and database-driven applications.
Experience with JavaScript frameworks and libraries (such as React, jQuery, OpenLayers, and Leaflet), and strong proficiency with HTML/CSS.
Experience with Python and PHP.
Experience with databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL).
Experience with security concepts.
Experience with collaboration software.
Excellent interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Well-versed in software engineering methodology and processes.
Ability to obtain and maintain a national agency check and background investigation after hire to obtain credentials for facility access and user accounts.
Three years of continuous residency in the US for issuance of a Government Security credential.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with a cloud provider and cloud concepts (e.g., AWS or Azure).
Familiarity with Kubernetes or other container technologies.
Familiarity with requirements and design analysis.
Experience with testing and configuration management tools such as Git.
Experience with geospatial tools (commercial or open source), including analysis, visualization, or data handling workflows.
Knowledge of OGC standards (WMS, WFS, WCS, WPS) and OGC APIs.
Familiarity with projections, reference systems, and spatial data transformations.

Experience and/or education in lieu of these qualifications will be reviewed for applicability to meet these requirements.

Additional Information

Paying attention to who we are as a company–people, family members, friends, and colleagues–is our primary focus at Element 84. There are lots of ways to run a company, and, for us, we prioritize wanting to come to work, being around people we enjoy, taking on big things with people you trust, and sharing our achievements as a team.

You'll get credit when things go right and we'll have your back when things go wrong.
We only take on work that is challenging and right for us. There are projects we will turn down and the team has a say.
We may be a small company, but we have big company benefits meant to support the idea that we're here for the long term and happiness comes from much more than where you work.
We have an extraordinary retention rate because we hire extraordinary people. We hope that's you.

Newsweek Recognizes Sedgwick as America’s Greatest Workplaces National Top Companies

Application Developer - Security Engineering

Primary Purpose

Designs, develops, and maintains applications, integrations, and automation that support enterprise security operations. Partners with Security Operations, IAM, Cloud Engineering, and Enterprise Architecture to turn detection and response requirements into working software. Builds and tunes content within the organization’s SIEM platform, develops data pipelines that feed it, and automates response workflows. Applies secure-by-default engineering practices, least privilege, and documented change control to everything delivered.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Application development

Develops, tests, and maintains applications, APIs, and services supporting security operations and compliance reporting.
Writes code that follows secure development standards, including input validation, output encoding, secrets management through an approved vault, and dependency scanning in the build pipeline.
Participates in peer code review, maintains unit and integration test coverage, and supports CI/CD pipelines for application and detection content releases.
Produces and maintains technical documentation, including design decisions, data flows, interface contracts, and runbooks with named ownership.

SIEM engineering and detection content

Builds, tests, and tunes SIEM detection rules, correlation searches, dashboards, and scheduled reports.
Develops and maintains log ingestion pipelines: source onboarding, parsing, field extraction, normalization to a common schema, and enrichment.
Troubleshoots ingestion gaps, parsing failures, licensing and volume issues, and data quality problems affecting detection reliability.
Manages detection content as code in version control, with documented test cases, promotion through non-production environments, and rollback procedures.
Maps detection coverage to a recognized framework such as MITRE ATT&CK and reports coverage gaps to Security leadership.

Automation and integration

Develops integrations between the SIEM and adjacent platforms, including EDR, identity, ticketing, vulnerability management, and cloud-native security services.
Builds SOAR playbooks and automation scripts that reduce manual analyst effort, with approval gates on any action that is destructive or privileged.
Instruments applications and infrastructure for security-relevant logging and validates that required audit events reach the SIEM.

Governance and collaboration

Works with Security, Cloud Engineering, IAM, and application teams to gather requirements and validate that delivered tooling meets operational need.
Supports audit and compliance evidence requests related to logging, monitoring, and alerting controls.
Follows enterprise change management for all production changes, including approvals, testing evidence, and defined back-out plans.
Participates in an on-call or escalation rotation for critical security tooling.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
Four or more years of professional software development experience.
Two or more years working directly with a SIEM platform, Google Security Operations (Google SecOps) preferred; comparable experience with Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Elastic Security, or IBM QRadar considered.
Proficiency writing SIEM query and detection logic — for example YARA-L 2.0 in Google SecOps, or KQL, SPL, or an equivalent query language — including performance tuning of scheduled rules and searches.
Strong programming skills in at least one of Python, C#/.NET, Java, or Go, plus scripting with PowerShell or Bash.
Working knowledge of REST API development and consumption, JSON, authentication patterns including OAuth 2.0, and webhook-based integration.
Experience with Git-based version control and CI/CD pipelines.
Practical understanding of core security concepts: authentication and authorization, encryption in transit and at-rest, logging and audit requirements, least privilege, and common attack techniques.
Demonstrated ability to document assumptions, dependencies, and operational ownership for delivered work.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on Google SecOps engineering experience, including UDM (Unified Data Model) normalization, parser and parser-extension development, log forwarder and ingestion API onboarding, data RBAC, reference lists, and Applied Threat Intelligence or curated detection content.
Experience with log pipeline and routing tools such as Cribl, Logstash, Fluent Bit, or Kafka.
Detection-as-code practices, including Sigma rules, automated detection testing, and content promotion pipelines.
SOAR development experience, Google SecOps SOAR (formerly Siemplify) preferred; Microsoft Sentinel playbooks, Splunk SOAR, or Cortex XSOAR also considered. Includes playbook design, custom integration and action development in Python, and case management workflow configuration.
Cloud security engineering in Azure or AWS, including native logging services, managed identities, and private networking patterns; working familiarity with Google Cloud a plus given the SecOps platform.
Infrastructure as code with Terraform or Bicep.
Experience supporting regulated data environments and control frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, or NIST CSF.
Relevant certifications, for example Google Cloud Professional Security Engineer, Google SecOps platform training or credentials, Microsoft SC-200, GIAC GCDA or GCIA, CompTIA Security+, or CISSP.
Experience with containerized workloads and Kubernetes.

Core Competencies

Translates security requirements into maintainable software rather than one-off scripts.
Communicates technical risk clearly to operations, engineering, and non-technical stakeholders.
Exercises judgment about blast radius before acting on production systems.
Works effectively across security, infrastructure, and application teams with competing priorities.
Maintains confidentiality when handling sensitive security, customer, or employee data.

Work environment

When applicable and appropriate, consideration will be given to reasonable accommodation.
Mental: Clear and conceptual thinking ability; excellent judgment, troubleshooting, problem solving, analysis, and discretion; ability to handle work-related stress; ability to handle multiple priorities simultaneously; and ability to meet deadlines
Physical: Computer keyboarding, travel as required
Auditory/Visual: Hearing, vision and talking

The Role

We are hiring an AI Automation Engineer who thrives on building durable, fast-moving solutions that unlock operational efficiency and connect people, processes, and tools across the functions that run the company.

In this role, you will serve as a hands-on builder and cross-functional partner, working with leaders and process owners across finance and operations to design and implement AI-powered workflows that make our teams more effective. You will focus on using tools like Claude and Claude Code, N8N, Glean, and direct API work against NetSuite, Salesforce, and Snowflake to automate, integrate, and scale how we work without needing to reinvent the wheel.

This is not a traditional engineering role. It is ideal for someone who loves solving complex problems at the intersection of technology and business operations, a true solutions engineer who is just as comfortable connecting APIs as sitting with an accountant to learn why a process works the way it does. You will also work closely with the AI Champions and builders already embedded across the business to align efforts, ensure adoption, and share best practices company-wide.

What You'll Do

Find the work
by partnering with process owners to map how work actually happens today, including the exceptions, the workarounds, and the steps that only live with a user. Much of the highest-value work will be work nobody filed a request for.
Size it before you build it
by defining the metric and stating the expected result up front, whether that is hours removed, cycle time, error rate, or cost avoided, then measuring the actual result once it ships.
Build and automate smart workflows
using AI agents and skills, API integrations, SQL and Python, workflow orchestration, and scripting against the systems where the work lives, taking each one from prototype to production.
Own the connective layer
by moving data cleanly between NetSuite, Salesforce, DealHub, Workday, Greenhouse, Snowflake, and the rest of the stack through APIs, webhooks, and pipelines, including the reconciliations that prove both sides agree.
Multiply the builders already in each function
by publishing the shared primitives, patterns, and templates they need, so capability compounds instead of queueing behind one person, and by maintaining the automation inventory, including retiring what no longer earns its place.

2-4+ years of experience in a technical, operations, or automation-focused role such as solutions engineering, business systems, RevOps, or technical program management..
Working proficiency in at least one scripting language, plus experience integrating systems via APIs, webhooks, and data flows.
Hands-on production experience with modern AI tooling such as Claude / Claude Code, Cursor, agent frameworks, MCP, or N8N, and informed opinions about when each is the wrong choice.
Real depth in at least one enterprise business system and its data model.
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills with the ability to translate business needs into clear, actionable technical solutions.
A builder's mindset that is creative, curious, and eager to experiment with new technologies to drive efficiency.
Excellent communication skills and comfort working with multiple stakeholders in a fast-moving environment.

What Makes You Stand Out

Experience in B2B SaaS, EdTech, or fintech industries.
Familiarity with scripting or data tools such as Python, JavaScript, or SQL for customization and troubleshooting.
Experience across a finance stack or a GTM stack (ERP, CRM, CPQ, support platforms).

Experience with hardware and laboratory bring-up processes.
Experience in test automation, refactoring code, test-driven development, build infrastructure, optimizing software, and debugging.
Experience with the Fuchsia operating system ecosystem or other operating systems.
Ability to communicate and work with others on technical projects.
Ability to prioritize requests from partner teams and triage technical issues.

About The Job

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

The Platforms and Devices team encompasses Google's various computing software platforms across environments (desktop, mobile, applications), as well as our first party devices and services that combine the best of Google AI, software, and hardware. Teams across this area research, design, and develop new technologies to make our user's interaction with computing faster and more seamless, building innovative experiences for our users around the world.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Deliver infrastructure to testing components and products based on knowledge of differences and considerations for each test phase (e.g., validity, verification, performance, reliability, usability, stress testing) and develop tests to test out infrastructure for each of the major phases of software development.
Build a suite of monitoring and anomaly detection tools which help us reduce our overall flakiness.
Improve the tooling used to identify latency during builds and find ways to improve stability.
Work closely with EngProd, TPM, Engineering, and Product Management teams to help deliver our infrastructure as a whole.
Generate the ideas required to solve technical problems and take full ownership of delivering the solution.

added.title: Software Engineer, iOS
added.description:
Our Mission

Launched in 2012, Tinder® revolutionized how people meet, growing from 1 match to one billion matches in just two years. This rapid growth demonstrates its ability to fulfill a fundamental human need: real connection. Today, the app has been downloaded over 630 million times, leading to over 97 billion matches, serving approximately 50 million users per month in 190 countries and 45+ languages - a scale unmatched by any other app in the category. In 2024, Tinder won four Effie Awards for its first-ever global brand campaign, “It Starts with a Swipe”™"

Our Values

One Team, One Dream

We work hand-in-hand, building Tinder for our members. We succeed together when we work collaboratively across functions, teams, and time zones, and think outside the box to achieve our company vision and mission.

Own It

We take accountability and strive to make a positive impact in all aspects of our business, through ownership, innovation, and a commitment to excellence.

Never Stop Learning

We cultivate a culture where it’s safe to take risks. We seek out input, share honest feedback, celebrate our wins, and learn from our mistakes in order to continue improving.

Spark Solutions

We’re problem solvers, focusing on how to best move forward when faced with obstacles. We don’t dwell on the past or on the issues at hand, but instead look at how to stay agile and overcome hurdles to achieve our goals.

Embrace Our Differences

We are intentional about building a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of our members. By leveraging different perspectives and other ways of thinking, we build better experiences for our members and our team.

As an iOS engineer at Tinder, you will have an outsized impact and ownership of the most visible aspects of the Tinder App. We are deeply invested in challenging norms, constantly improving architecture design, exploring emergent tech and ideas, and leveraging new technologies in interesting ways to deliver an app that is widely known across the world.

Where You’ll Work

This is a hybrid role and requires in-office collaboration three times per week in our Palo Alto, CA office.

In This Role, You Will

Contribute to the architecture, design and implementation of consumer facing features in the Tinder App
Build compelling in-app experiences that will reach millions of users globally
Collaborate with engineers cross-functionally as well as the product and design team(s) to influence the roadmap and product development of Tinder’s App and services
Contribute to internal shared frameworks and libraries
Shape the future of optimized analytics at Tinder from the ground up with innovative data tools for the analytics and data science team(s)
Evolve Tinder’s architecture to support multiple authentication flows and account management
Mentor, collaborate, and learn from innovative and passionate team members

You'll Need

2+ years of experience building consumer-facing applications with native iOS
Full life cycle experience building applications in Swift
Proficient in Swift concepts (structs, optionals, generics etc.)
Experience building user-facing features with autolayout
Familiar with popular architecture patterns such as MVVM / Clean and their uses
Knowledge of iOS memory management and protocol-oriented programming
Experience building and testing large-scale iOS apps and/or codebases
Proficiency writing your own unit tests
Clear and solutions oriented communication style with a passion for code quality
Willingness to work collaboratively in an Agile environment (scrum, planning poker, standup, etc.)

Nice To Have

Experience with building public APIs and mobile SDK’s
Knowledge of native iOS frameworks like URL Session, Core Data and Core Animation
Comfortable working with legacy code and improving it
Experience communicating and implementing effective, solutions oriented improvements
Familiar with implementing In-App Purchases, StoreKit or implementing premium features in an iOS app
A BS or MS in Computer Science or Engineering is amazing but not required; proficiency in modern iOS technologies and principles is what matters most

As a Full Time Employee, You'll Enjoy

Flexible Vacation, 10 Sick Days
Time off to volunteer and charitable donations matched up to $15,000 annually
Comprehensive health, vision, and dental coverage
100% 401(k) employer match up to 10%, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
100% paid parental leave (including for non-birthing parents) and family forming benefits
Investment in your development: mentorship through our MentorMatch program, access to 6,000+ online courses through Udemy, and an annual $3,000 stipend for your professional development
Investment in your wellness: access to mental health support via Modern Health, paid concierge medical membership, pet insurance, fitness membership subsidy, and commuter subsidy
Free subscription to Tinder Gold

Commitment to Inclusion

At Tinder, we don’t just accept difference, we celebrate it. We strive to build a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of our members around the world, and we value unique perspectives and backgrounds. Even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications, we invite you to apply and show us how your skills could transfer. Tinder is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace where we welcome people of all sexes, gender identities, races, ethnicities, disabilities, and other lived experiences. Learn more here: https://www.lifeattinder.com/dei

If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please speak to your Talent Acquisition Partner directly.

#Tinder

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

The salary range for this position is $165,000 - 185,000. Factors such as scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, job-related skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and business considerations may influence base pay offered. This salary range is reflective of a position based in Los Angeles. This salary will be subject to a geographic adjustment (according to a specific city and state), if an authorization is granted to work outside of the location listed in this posting.

added.title: Cloud Data Platform Engineer
added.description:
For decades, DTN has been the silent force behind some of the world’s most critical industries—helping businesses navigate complexity, uncertainty, and risk with smarter, faster decisions. From agriculture to energy to weather intelligence, our proprietary Operational Decisioning Platform transforms raw data into decision-grade insights—enabling companies to optimize supply chains, ensure market stability, and safeguard infrastructure against disruption. We don’t follow trends—we set the standard for precision, trust, and operational impact.

DTN is at an exciting inflection point. Building off a foundation of financial strength, profitability, and industry trust, we’re accelerating growth and expanding our global footprint. Our purpose-built solutions—powered by AI and honed by decades of vertical expertise—are helping some of the world’s most significant enterprises thrive amid operational constraints and uncover new opportunities in a fast-changing world.

J
ob Description:

Position Summary:

DTN is seeking a talented Platform Engineer
to help build and evolve the foundational cloud-native capabilities of our Operational Decisioning Platform (ODP).

The DTN Operational Decisioning Platform is an internal platform that packages cloud infrastructure into purpose-built, higher-level capabilities so that our engineers, solutions teams, and customers can build data products, applications, and AI-powered tools without managing the underlying cloud infrastructure themselves.

As a Platform Engineer, you will build and deliver features across the platform's developer-facing APIs, software development kits (SDKs), command-line interfaces (CLIs), module framework, and managed services. You will work autonomously on well-scoped engineering initiatives while collaborating with senior engineers who provide technical guidance, design reviews, and mentorship.

This is an opportunity for an engineer with several years of professional experience to deepen their expertise in AWS cloud-native technologies, distributed systems, and platform engineering. You will help build infrastructure that other engineers depend on while developing the technical judgment and ownership skills needed to advance toward a senior engineering role.

What You Will Be Responsible For:

Platform Feature Development and Delivery

Design, build, test, and deploy platform features from initial planning through production delivery.
Implement service logic, module functionality, and business logic supporting the DTN Operational Decisioning Platform.
Develop and extend developer-facing APIs, SDKs, CLIs, and managed platform capabilities.
Write and maintain infrastructure-as-code configurations required to provision and deploy platform services.
Independently own moderately complex engineering features from development through deployment, with minimal oversight.
Solve day-to-day technical challenges independently while escalating architectural and design questions to senior engineers when appropriate.

Module Framework and Distributed Systems

Contribute to the development and evolution of the platform's module framework.
Implement interface contracts and business logic within a framework that manages common platform requirements.
Work with framework capabilities supporting authentication, authenticated communication, dispatch, validation, metrics, retries, and reconciliation.
Develop reliable software components that integrate effectively with the platform's shared services and architectural standards.
Apply distributed-systems principles, including asynchronous processing, retry handling, idempotency, and reliable service interactions.
Contribute to modular, reusable platform capabilities that enable other engineering teams to build applications and data products without directly managing underlying cloud infrastructure.

Software Quality and Engineering Practices

Develop reliable, maintainable, and thoroughly tested production software.
Create and maintain automated unit and integration tests to validate application functionality and system behavior.
Use established build tooling, continuous integration processes, and automated testing practices.
Follow trunk-based development practices to keep code changes deployable and support incremental delivery.
Apply established platform standards for security, interface design, infrastructure as code, and software development.
Participate in technical design discussions and code reviews, incorporating feedback to continuously improve engineering quality.
Use version control and source-management practices to support effective collaboration and reliable software delivery.

Cloud Infrastructure and Operational Support

Develop and maintain cloud-native services using AWS infrastructure and platform capabilities.
Work with cloud compute, storage, identity and access management, API services, managed data stores, and event-driven technologies.

Job Description

This contract role focuses on developing, enhancing, and supporting software solutions for automated laboratory and industrial systems. The Software Engineer will design and implement software that integrates instrumentation, machine vision, data acquisition, and enterprise data systems to improve the efficiency, quality, and scalability of research and operational processes. The position supports global automation initiatives across seed production innovation and product supply, working closely with multidisciplinary teams to deliver robust software and automation solutions for research, testing, and operational workflows.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, test, and maintain software for engineering and laboratory systems used in research, testing, and operational environments.
Develop applications using C#, MATLAB, Python, and related technologies to support automation, data processing, and system control.
Create integration and processing software that connects instrumentation, sensors, automation systems, databases, cloud platforms, and enterprise applications.
Collaborate closely with scientists, engineers, and technicians to gather detailed requirements and translate them into effective software and automation solutions.
Troubleshoot software and system integration issues, diagnosing problems across hardware, software, and network interfaces and implementing durable fixes.
Develop clear technical documentation, including software specifications, architecture descriptions, and user guides to support implementation and ongoing maintenance.
Follow modern software engineering best practices, including the use of version control, unit testing, code reviews, change management, and structured release and deployment processes.
Work with internal engineering teams, seed production innovation groups, product supply personnel, and external contractors, suppliers, and equipment vendors to ensure successful delivery and support of automation systems.

Essential Skills

Bachelors or Masters degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, Automation Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
At least 3 years of full-time professional experience developing software for automation, industrial, scientific, IT, or engineering systems.
Strong programming skills in C# and the .NET ecosystem, including experience with .NET Framework, .NET, WPF, WinForms, or relevant application frameworks.
Proficiency in C#, MATLAB, Python, or similar programming languages for application development and data processing.
Hands-on experience integrating software with hardware systems such as instrumentation, sensors, machine vision systems, robotics, or industrial control platforms.
Experience using version control tools and applying modern software engineering practices, including software testing and structured development workflows.
Demonstrated analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capabilities in complex, multidisciplinary technical environments.
Ability to work full-time on-site at research facilities in St. Louis, Missouri.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Experience in developing software for laboratory systems, imaging systems, or industrial automation environments.
Experience working within multidisciplinary teams that include scientists, engineers, technicians, and operations personnel.
Familiarity with integrating software solutions with databases, cloud platforms, and enterprise applications.
Ability to produce high-quality technical documentation and user guides for diverse technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong communication skills to effectively collaborate with internal teams and external contractors, suppliers, and equipment vendors.

added.title: Software Engineer, State Estimation & Localization
added.description:
Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

We’re looking for a Software Engineer
to develop the state-estimation systems that allow autonomous machines to understand their position, orientation, motion, and configuration. You’ll build production software that combines data from GNSS, IMUs, lidar, cameras, encoders, and other sources, to not only estimate the state of the machine but also the surrounding environment which the machines themselves are actively reshaping.

Accurate state estimation is essential to both safety and performance. Your work will help our machines operate precisely, recognize when sensor data or estimates are unreliable, and respond safely when inputs are delayed, degraded, or unavailable.

Depending on your background, you may focus on real-time sensor fusion, estimator reliability, SLAM, offline optimization, or calibration. This is a hands-on role spanning algorithm design, production software, data analysis, and testing on real machines.

What You’ll Do

Design, implement, and deploy state-estimation and localization algorithms for autonomous construction machines
Combine GNSS, IMU, lidar, and machine-sensor data into accurate, real-time estimates of machine position, motion, and configuration
Improve reliability through sensor monitoring, consistency checks, fault detection, trustworthy confidence estimates, redundancy, and graceful degradation
Handle measurements that arrive late, out of order, intermittently, or not at all
Build ground-truth systems, offline reference estimators, metrics, and regression tests that measure performance and expose failures
Build metrics for fleet wide monitoring of pose and calibration accuracy
Work on related problems such as sensor calibration, clock synchronization, lidar-based arm estimation, and joint offline estimation
Diagnose issues using field data, recorded-data replay, and simulation, then test improvements on physical machines
Collaborate with controls, perception, safety, hardware, and systems teams to improve the performance of the complete autonomy system

What We're Looking For

4+ years of professional engineering or applied research experience in state estimation, localization, navigation, SLAM, or sensor fusion
Strong foundations in probabilistic estimation, linear algebra, 3D geometry, and numerical methods
Hands-on experience with one or more of GNSS/INS fusion, Kalman filtering, factor graphs, lidar or visual odometry, point-cloud registration, or sensor calibration
Strong production software skills in Rust or modern C++. Our production stack is primarily Rust, and we will support experienced C++ engineers as they ramp up
Experience measuring estimator performance using ground truth, recorded data, simulation, and real-world testing
Strong debugging and data-analysis skills, including the ability to investigate problems across algorithms, software, sensors, and hardware
A degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Ways To Stand Out

Experience deploying state-estimation systems on autonomous vehicles, robots, or embedded platforms
Experience with estimator monitoring, uncertainty, fault detection, redundancy, or safety-relevant systems
Experience with nonlinear optimization, factor graphs, or smoothing
Deep knowledge of GNSS, inertial sensing, lidar, sensor timing, calibration, and real-world failure modes
Experience with lidar localization, ICP, continuous-time estimation, or articulated-machine estimation
Experience building offline reference estimators or independent ground-truth systems
Production experience with Rust
Familiarity with construction, mining, agricultural, or other heavy industrial machines

Other Special Aspects Of The Role

Based in the Bay Area with the ability to be onsite at our SF office on a daily/weekly basis

Job Summary

Designs, fabricates, modifies, evaluates and documents molded assemblies, components, and systems to produce or improve company products and facilitate manufacturing operations. Develops data and makes preliminary sketches, lay-outs and notes required to present design proposals. Researches basic design factors such as ease of manufacture and availability of materials and equipment. Works with other organizations impacted by design development.

May perform work in a specific sub-specialty such as Automation, Mechanical Engineering, Mold Design, or Tooling. Please see addendum for specific sub-specialty requirements. This description is designed to capture the general elements of Engineering work.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Design and develops plastic molded sub-assemblies, components, and packaging as assigned.
Develops and implements changes to product design and/or the manufacturing process to achieve efficiency, quality, and/or cost improvements by participating in new product development programs.
Develops requirement specifications, system concepts, CAD generated machine layouts, detail drawings, BOM’s and budgets. Makes layouts of basic and some complex assemblies and details of parts of devices, mechanisms and structures.
Provides customer product design engineering for economic production; may participate in meetings with customers.
Assesses proper material, tooling, automation and equipment selection.
Works with manufacturing to trouble-shoot problems, upgrades, retrofits, set-ups, methods development, and the development of process parameters
Participates in product development meetings and may make recommendations to product design changes to enhance manufacturing and assembly.
May conduct proof of concept experiments and design other testing requirements as needed.
May develop SOP’s, operations and maintenance manuals.
May research new technology or development tools to remain informed of current technology.
Understanding of Lean Six Sigma tools, projects and processes and ability to incorporate these into assigned engineering projects.
Reviews completed projects for accuracy, clarity and completeness.
Supports all company safety and quality programs and initiatives.
May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Engineering Addendum

Automation

Technical responsibility for design and development of automation requirement specification and systems concepts and installs automation and transfer automation programs to production in a smooth and timely manner.

CAD/CAE

Technical responsibility for design and production of 2D and 3D representations of plastic injection molded assemblies, components, packaging and products.

Mechanical

Technical responsibility for a variety of engineering work in planning and design of products, tools, engines, machines and other mechanically functioning equipment and mechanical industrial processes; oversees production, installation, operation, maintenance and repair of such equipment.

Materials

Technical responsibility for the manipulation of the molecular structure of substances used to create new material for use in products, specifically working with plastics or composites that meet certain mechanical, chemical and electrical requirements. Responsible for determining test and performance requirements. Develops test methodologies and procedures and tests materials as required.

Mold Design

Technical responsibility for the design and development of molds used to produce plastic assemblies, components and packaging involving environmental, mechanical and thermal limitations. May design and build prototypes. May conduct mold qualifications and validations on new molds using various experiments. Involves robust knowledge of scientific molding methodologies.

Packaging

Technical responsibility for the design and development of packing materials, shipping containers, etc., for attractive and safe shipping of products under varying conditions of climate and environment, and differing modes of transportation, using lubricants, protective material, and other methods as required

Tooling

Technical responsibility for designing a broad range of tools, including cutting and forming tools; designs jigs, dies, and fixtures for production or experimental use; resolves design problems related to material characteristics, dimensional tolerances, service requirements, manufacturing procedures and processes and costs. Applies standard mathematical formulas and standard tool engineering data to develop tool configuration and selects standard items for incorporation into tool design. Draws preliminary sketches and prepares layout and detail drawings. Modifies tool designs according to test or production service data to improve tool life or performance.

Job Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS

Understands processes and has a basic understanding of various manufacturing techniques
Basic knowledge of engineering theories, design principles and practices, and design evaluation techniques.
Proficiency in use of personal computers, Microsoft Office products (Excel, Word and PowerPoint) and e-mail skills required.

Education And Minimum Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Automation Engineering, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in automation engineering within a manufacturing environment, preferably in the plastics molding or medical device industry.
Proficiency in PLC programming (e.g., Allen-Bradley, Siemens) and HMI development.
Experience with industrial robotics (e.g., Fanuc, ABB, Universal Robots).
Strong understanding of industrial control systems, sensors, actuators, and vision systems.
Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex automation issues.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.
Familiarity with lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement methodologies is a plus.
Or equivalent combination of education, certifications and experience

added.title: Software Engineer, AI Infra
added.description:
About Eventual

Robots and world models learn about the physical world from video: millions of hours of people cooking, building, carrying and fixing things. That footage is piling up faster than anyone can review it, and much of it is mislabeled, out of sync or not useful for training. Most teams still choose what to train on by having people watch a small sample. When a model learns from bad examples, it learns the wrong behavior.

Eventual
is building data curation for Physical AI. We process video and sensor data at petabyte scale and extract signals from it: how hands and objects interact, what happens over time (a failed grasp, a retry, a recovery) and whether a clip is reliable enough to learn from. Leading Physical AI labs and robotics teams use these signals to decide what goes into their next training run.

The work spans large-scale data systems, computer vision and ML research, and it ships directly into how frontier models get trained. We’re a small team from AWS, Lyft and Tesla, backed by $30M from Felicis, CRV, Y Combinator and the co-founders of Databricks and Perplexity. We helped power the last generation of Physical AI in self-driving, and now we’re building what the next generation trains on.

Join our small (but powerful!) team, 4 days/week in our SF Mission District office.

Our Mission:

Our goal is to build Scenario Mining and Data Curation for robot fleet data. We empower Physical AI and robotics teams to instantly find, curate, and stream the data they need to train frontier models.

Eventual is an agile team where every engineer has high ownership across the stack from our compute infrastructure, to our data storage/querying layers and model training/deployment.

Your Role:

As a Software Engineer on the AI Infra team, you will build the storage, query and ML infrastructure behind our platform. The systems you build have two sets of users:

External customers use our platform to search their data, visualize signals, query through agents and MCP, and export curated datasets for training.
Our applied research team ingests new datasets, experiments with new features, and then uses our storage and compute infrastructure to produce those features as signals at scale.

You will build systems that let researchers go from a new dataset to a production signal quickly, and that customers can rely on to find and pull the data they need. We operate as a tight-knit, experienced engineering team that values technical autonomy, deep execution, and owning problems end to end.

Key Responsibilities

Multimodal Storage (Data Lake): Build our data lake on modern columnar formats (Apache Parquet, Apache Iceberg etc) for video, lidar, sensor logs and the signals derived from them.
Query Engine: Build querying capabilities for both customers and researchers. Our multi-stage query systems use partitioning, indexing, embeddings/vector search for search and retrieval, and LLMs/VLMs for perception-based query predicates. These are exposed through our UI, APIs and agent/MCP interfaces.
ML Infrastructure: Build the platform that takes a research feature from experiment to production signal: fast dataset ingestion, GPU inference at scale, backfills across the full corpus, and versioning of models and signals.

What we look for

Proven track record building ML platforms or robotics data platforms, such as training/inference pipelines, large-scale batch inference, feature/embedding stores, or tooling for finding and curating robot or autonomy data.
3+ years of experience building and operating large-scale data or ML infrastructure in production.
Experience with distributed compute and GPU workloads, plus practical exposure to scaling cloud infrastructure (AWS S3). Bonus points for experience with video decoding, vector search, or building agent/MCP interfaces over data.
High agency and adaptability to thrive in an autonomous, fast-paced startup environment building cutting-edge infrastructure for frontier robotics.

Competitive comp and startup equity
Catered lunches and dinners for SF employees
Commuter benefit
Team building events & poker nights
Health, vision, and dental coverage

Molex is seeking a motivated Software Engineer, Developer Productivity (AI Agents), to join our Optical Systems Business Unit in Fremont, California. The ideal candidate brings strong fundamentals in Python and software testing, and hands-on experience with AI coding agents. You will collaborate with firmware, hardware and test engineering teams across multiple time zones to build tools that help engineers use AI coding agents with confidence.

Molex brings a rich heritage in the optical industry, with the highest performing and field-proven solutions spanning components, modules and integrated line-cards. Our comprehensive optical, mechanical, electrical and software design capabilities allow us to serve the high-density, high-bandwidth and flexible networking needs of hyperscale datacenter, datacom and telecom customers. Continuous innovation in component integration, miniaturization and manufacturing automation keeps our products at the leading edge of optical networking.

Compare AI models and tools on quality, speed and cost, and summarize the results

Learn how firmware is developed, reviewed and released, and how it controls optical hardware
